# Brief 33: making the Vivado part of a run faster (measurements, 2026-11-11)

Vivado 2025.2 on the build PC (i7-3770, 4 cores / 8 threads, 32 GB, SATA SSD), one build at a time in heavy slot 1
("Vivado impl"). Another session's simulation (Icarus, one core) ran throughout, so every number carries that load;
`measure.sh` waits for any other Vivado to finish before each build (`waited ... s` lines in the logs).

**The numbers are in [results.md](results.md)** (and `summary.json`), generated by `summarise.py` from `raw/<label>/`.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `measure.sh` | runs one jobs file, one build at a time, and copies each build's records into `raw/<label>/` |
| `jobs_*.txt` | the jobs, in the order run: `jobs_batch1.txt` (small and mid designs at 1, 2, 4 threads twice, then the cached sequences), `jobs_c13seq.txt` (the mid sequence again: its first attempt was refused because another session's Vivado probe was running; those records were deleted), `jobs_inc*.txt` (incremental), `jobs_rig.txt` (the CDC rig at 2, 4, 1 threads) |
| `batch*.log` | the runs' own logs (batch 2 was stopped after the licence check when the other Vivado appeared; batch 3 repeated its work) |
| `raw/<label>/` | `call.json` (wall time of the call, thread count, cache decision, WNS, gates), `run.json`, `gates.json`, `stages.txt` (cumulative seconds per flow step), `result_hash.json`, `incremental_reuse.rpt` |
| rig records | after the runs, each rig `timing_summary.rpt` (1.6 MB) was cut to its first 160 lines (`timing_summary_head.rpt`, which holds the Design Timing Summary that `call.json`'s WNS came from) and `stdout.txt` was gzipped |
| `hash_dcp.tcl` | open saved checkpoints and write their result dumps (the rig) |
| `raw/t1_*` | the ILA variant started from the base build's post_synth.dcp, against a fresh ILA build (`designs/t1_dimmer_counter`) |
| `licence_check.sh`, `.tcl`, `.log` | Vivado with every licence hidden (HOME an empty directory, no licence variables) synthesising, placing and routing a counter on xc7a100t, xc7z020 and xck26 |

## Designs

- **small:** `c10_dds_sine` reference (benchmark/course dev split), 1.2k LUT, staged by `benchmark/tools/ref_build.py --stage-only`;
- **mid:** `c13_nexys_harris_vga` reference (dev split), 11k LUT, staged the same way; `c13_inc` is a copy of it for the
  incremental runs (its own path, so its build stamp and netlist differ slightly from `c13_nexys_harris_vga`);
- **large:** the CDC soak rig, full build (`hil/cdc_soak/run_build.sh full`), 36k LUT (56%); its own build script.

Small and mid builds ran with `FDA_RESULT_HASH=1` (placement and routing hashes) and `MEM_MAX=8G`.

**Result hashes, two versions.** The small and mid builds were hashed with the first version of the dump and hash
(every net segment written; the SHA-256 of the sorted lines). On the CDC rig that dump was 10 GB, took 658 s inside the
build and pushed the scope's anonymous memory to 11.6 GB of its 12 GB cap, and hashing it in memory was unsafe, so that
first rig attempt was stopped and its records kept apart (`raw_discarded/rig_t2_first_attempt_with_dump/`, not used in
any table). The committed version writes only the top segment of each net, in chunks, and hashes line by line (the sum
of each line's SHA-256 modulo 2^256, independent of order). The rig was then built without the dump, its
`post_route.dcp` saved, and hashed afterwards with `hash_dcp.tcl`, so its times and memory are the build's own. The
ILA check (`t1_*`) used the committed version. Hashes are compared only within one version.

## Licence check

All three parts synthesised, placed and routed with no licence file visible to Vivado (`licence_check.log`: Vivado
reports getting its synthesis and implementation licence for each device from the no-cost edition). A control with a
device outside the no-cost edition was not possible: this installation has only the no-cost device set (Zynq
UltraScale+ up to ZU7, xck24/xck26, no Virtex UltraScale+). The `foreach` list in `licence_check.tcl` was made
overridable (`LC_PARTS`) after the run; the default list is the one that ran.
